screens_reviewed: Single full-height capture of the Reports tab (light theme) on an Android tablet in portrait: header, two metric cards, Current report card with score + progress bar + CTA, a single-item Report list, and a web-dashboard footnote, over a bottom tab bar.
verdict: The screen is clean, readable, and functionally complete, with correct use of the shared ScaledText/ScaledParagraph primitives and the responsive content-container helper. However it is a phone layout scaled onto a tablet canvas: it never branches on layout.isTablet, so there is no list-detail/two-column adaptation, and body typography stays at phone point sizes because the TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE constant is never consumed. The result is usable but leaves a lot of empty vertical space and reads small for the device class.

improvements.location: app/(tabs)/reports.tsx (whole component; only layout use is getResponsiveContentContainerStyle at lines 66-69)
improvements.suggestion: Adapt to the tablet canvas with a list-detail split: render the focused 'Current report' card as a detail pane beside the 'Report list' (e.g. an XStack with twoPaneGap when layout.isTablet/isWideTablet), instead of stacking one full-width column. The route currently never reads layout.isTablet, so wide screens just stretch the phone stack and leave large empty space (visible in the screenshot below the footnote).
improvements.evidence: reports.tsx:33-50 builds focusedSubmission + sortedAudits but renders them as one vertical YStack (lines 130-327); image shows a single centered column with unused canvas

improvements.suggestion: ScaledText/ScaledParagraph multiply only by the user fontScale preference (scaleSize at ScaledText.tsx:2285-2287), never by TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE (1.3) defined for exactly this purpose. On tablet the body copy ('View submitted audit results...', timestamps, helper text) therefore renders at phone sizes and reads small against the large screen. Fold the tablet base scale into the scaled primitives (or pass it through useDesignSystem.fontScale) so default tablet text is sized up.
improvements.evidence: ScaledText.tsx:2296,2313 read only fontScale; TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE declared at responsive-layout-tokens.ts:792 but no consumer; image shows small body text with wide whitespace

improvements.suggestion: The metric value uses style={{ color: accentColor }} where accentColor for 'Average score' is designSystem.colors.primary (#10231F, a near-black). It reads fine, but the 'Top score' value uses colors.success (#5E9C83) at 30px headingBold; large-text AA (3:1) is met, just confirm it stays >=3:1 on the #FFFFFF surface. Prefer passing color as a prop consistent with the other ScaledText usages rather than mixing an inline style object.
improvements.evidence: reports.tsx:377 style={{ color: accentColor }} vs color={...} prop elsewhere (e.g. line 385); success #5E9C83 from lib/design-system.ts:310

improvements.suggestion: Android large-screen guidance favors a navigation rail over a bottom tab bar on tablets. The layout keeps a bottom Tabs bar at all widths (only icon size / label size change via layout.isTablet at _layout.tsx:1448,1459). Consider a left nav rail for tablet widths to follow Material large-screen conventions and free vertical space.
improvements.evidence: app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx uses expo-router Tabs with tabBarStyle (lines 1471-1483); no rail branch

tamagui_notes: reports.tsx correctly uses the shared ScaledText/ScaledParagraph primitives (imported as Text/Paragraph at reports.tsx:14) rather than raw tamagui Text/Paragraph, matching design_system_components_used.

Spacing uses tamagui $space tokens (gap="$4", p="$4", gap="$3") and radii come from designSystem.radii (lib/design-system.ts:415-429); no hard-coded magic paddings on this screen except intentional pixel sizes for progress-bar heights (10/6px, reports.tsx:193,290).

Content centering relies on getResponsiveContentContainerStyle (reports.tsx:66) with no maxWidth override, so it defaults to contentMaxWidth (1040-1200) and centers via adaptive gutters — correct usage of the helper.
Header 'Reports' is hand-styled inline (fontSize 32 / headingBold, reports.tsx:73-81) rather than using the shared ScreenHeader primitive (core.md:2325); minor consistency point, not a defect.
platform_notes: Android nav bar is hidden app-wide via useHiddenAndroidNavBar (core.md:1069-1091) and the screenshot shows no system nav bar overlapping the tab bar; bottom inset is folded into getResponsiveTabBarLayout (responsive-layout.ts:703-718).

Status bar at top ('10:07' row) is cleared: Stack contentStyle adds paddingTop:20 (app/_layout.tsx:1378) and ScrollView uses contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior="automatic" (reports.tsx:64); the screen does not pass topInset to the container helper but no clipping is visible.
Primary CTAs ('Open selected report', 'Open report') use tamagui Button default height and appear >=48dp tall in the capture — meets Android tap-target minimum.
Icons are Feather (components/icons.tsx); FileBarChart/BarChart3 both map to 'bar-chart-2' and TriangleAlert to 'alert-triangle' — no iOS-only chevrons rendered on this screen.
not_assessable: Exact WCAG contrast ratios for success-green (#5E9C83) score text on #FFFFFF surface — estimated to pass large-text AA but not measured.
Empty state ('No submitted audits yet', reports.tsx:106-128) and pending_upload sync styling are not exercised in this capture (data shows one uploaded report).
Landscape / split-view behavior and whether the single-column stack reflows acceptably at wider tablet widths cannot be judged from one portrait screenshot.
Whether selecting a place elsewhere correctly drives focusedSubmission highlighting (cross-screen selection-store flow) is out of scope for this single screen.
score_rationale: Solid and shippable: correct shared-primitive usage, token-based spacing, safe handling of Android system bars, and adequate tap targets, with no critical defects. It loses points for being a phone layout on a tablet canvas — no list-detail/multi-column adaptation despite available data, and the defined TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE is never applied so text reads small with large unused space. These are polish/adaptation gaps rather than breakage, landing it at a 7.
